stage_2_story.text_en:
On Thursday afternoon, David went to the supermarket to buy groceries for the week. He took a large cart at the entrance because his list was long. First, he headed to the produce section to pick up tomatoes, cucumbers, and a bag of apples. He always checked the expiry date on the packaged salads before putting them in the cart.

Next, he walked down the dairy aisle and found that yogurt was on a big discount — buy two, get one free. He grabbed three packs. On the shelf above the yogurt, he spotted a new brand of cheese and decided to try it.

After collecting everything on his list, David remembered he had two coupons in his wallet — one for bread and one for orange juice. He made sure to bring both items so he could use the coupons at the checkout.

At the checkout, a friendly cashier scanned all the items and applied the coupons. The total came to sixty-two shekels less than David had expected. He paid, took his bags, and drove home feeling pleased. He had saved money and found everything he needed without any trouble.
